findings.title: The `shuttingDown` latch is never cleared, so after any session replacement the settle abort path silently parks instead of re-engaging
findings.detail: `let shuttingDown = false` is set to true in the `session_shutdown` handler (goal.ts:1192) and never reset anywhere; the only reader is the new guard in the settle abort path: `if (shuttingDown || stopped || !goal || goal.status !== "active") { updateFooter(); return undefined; }` (goal.ts:1396). Extension factories run once per process and the same handler closures are reused for later sessions: `session_shutdown` is emitted by `AgentSessionRuntime.teardownCurrent` for reason "new"/"resume"/"fork" (node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/agent-session-runtime.js:102-112), and the replacement session is built by `createAgentSessionFromServices` reusing `services.resourceLoader` (agent-session-services.js:129-141) and the same loaded extension objects (`_buildRuntime` → `resourceLoader.getExtensions()`, agent-session.js:2845,2862), so the closure survives while only its `session_start`/`session_tree` state is re-adopted (adoptBranchState, goal.ts:1143-1160). pi's own docs confirm this lifecycle: "Reconstruct branch-sensitive state ... during `session_start`" and cleanup "can converge on the same path" for "reload, session replacement, and process exit" (node_modules/.../docs/extensions.md:229,258-259). Consequence: after one /new, /resume, /fork or import in a process, every later alt+x kill of a settle check falls into the silent branch — the verify is killed but no notice is queued and no continuation is requested, i.e. the exact pre-change parking behaviour the diff set out to fix, with no visible signal (the README advertises the check as "killable mid-run (alt+x)"). Note the asymmetry: the diff carefully resets `parkedForTasks` in adoptBranchState/setGoal (goal.ts:1154,1176) but not this latch, and no test exercises a settle abort in a second session (the new test at tests/goal.test.ts:1519 only fires `session_shutdown` and then asserts the same-session silence).
findings.recommendation: Reset `shuttingDown = false` on the session's fresh start (in `adoptBranchState`, next to the other re-adoptions) — or clear it on the same `session_shutdown` microtask after the drain, since only the in-flight settle of that teardown must stay silent. Add a test that emits session_shutdown and then session_start and asserts a later kill still re-engages.

findings.title: The deferral's premise (a completion wake re-engages the agent) fails for never-ending or killed tasks, parking the goal loop
findings.detail: Still valid in this revision (same code, now reachable in production). The guard `const running = runningTasks(); if (running.length > 0) { setStatus/notify; return undefined; }` (goal.ts:1277-1297) returns before the continuation-cap/progress-judge block (goal.ts:1298+) and never touches `continuations`, so the park has no bound — no deferral counter, no wall-clock deadline, and the cap cannot end it. `TaskRegistry.running()` counts only `state === "running"` (lib/superbash.ts), `killTask` flips the state without delivering a wake, and `complete()` is fire-once, so a task that never exits (the subagents/bash docs advertise dev servers and watchers for background runs) or one killed while the loop is parked produces no wake at all. The new `Symbol.for` process-global holder (lib/superbash.ts:416-431) plus the publish in extensions/subagents.ts:1093 is exactly what makes this path live (the previous module-scoped holder never connected goal's reader to subagents' writer under pi's per-extension loader), so the goal's machine-checkable gate and its automatic continuation stop driving the objective for the entire lifetime of any running background task; the only signals are the footer `goal · holding check — N background tasks running` and the one-shot notice (goal.ts:1288-1295), and the notice itself concedes the recovery needs a user prompt ("the check then runs on your next prompt"). The added tests cover only defer→calm.
findings.recommendation: Bound the park instead of making it unconditional: record the first deferral (counter or timestamp) and after N deferrals or a grace deadline run the check anyway with a notice naming the still-running tasks, or have the registry surface kill/settle transitions so a killed or timed-out task triggers a settle rather than relying on a wake.

findings.title: The exit→close gap is a wall-clock proxy, so an event-loop stall between the two callbacks fails a passing verify
findings.detail: Carried over from the previous review and unchanged by this revision (the diff does not touch `runVerify`). `runVerify` decides a verify backgrounded its work partly by comparing timestamps stamped in two different libuv callbacks: `exitedAt = Date.now()` in `child.on("exit")` (goal.ts:397-398) and `const heldByDescendant = exitedAt !== undefined && Date.now() - exitedAt > EXIT_TO_CLOSE_GRACE_MS` (goal.ts:399, grace 250 ms) in `child.on("close")`. Any synchronous parent work between the two callbacks longer than the grace (another extension's CPU-bound handler, a large parse, a GC pause) makes `heldByDescendant` true for a foreground verify that exited 0, and the check is then graded as `spawnError: "verify left background processes running; a verify must run its check in the foreground and exit"` (goal.ts:401-414): a green check is reported as a failure at the settle boundary, the loop re-engages on that false failure, and `action: "complete"` refuses a goal that is in fact met. The companion probe `groupAlive(child.pid)` on the same line is sound (it queries the process group directly); only the clock comparison is a proxy, and no test synthesizes a stall between `exit` and `close`.
findings.recommendation: Keep `groupAlive(child.pid)` as the verdict and turn the timestamp gap into a bounded re-probe: after `close` with code 0, re-check `groupAlive` once after the grace window and fail only if a group member is still alive.

findings.title: parkedForTasks resets on /goal resume and on branch adoption are untested (only setGoal's is covered)
findings.detail: This diff introduces the same `parkedForTasks = false` reset at three sites: resetContinuationBudget (goal.ts:1140 — reached by /goal resume and a user kickoff), adoptBranchState (goal.ts:1154 — session_start/session_tree), and setGoal (goal.ts:1176). The new test only exercises the setGoal reset ("A model-set goal while still parked re-announces too", tests/goal.test.ts:1158-1162). No test parks the loop and then issues /goal resume or session_tree and asserts the "check held" notify fires again, so deleting either of the other two lines leaves the whole suite green while the re-armed/adopted goal silently re-parks with no notice. Recommendation: extend the deferral test to park, then `/goal resume` (and fire `session_tree`), and assert ctx.ui.notify is called again.

findings.title: The aborted check row reuses staleContinuations, so a row that says nothing was measured can also claim "measured N turn(s) ago"
findings.detail: The new aborted details set `staleContinuations: lastCheckAge` (goal.ts:1420) while `lastCheckAge` is the age of the previous cached measurement (incremented on the reuse path, goal.ts:1431-1432), and `renderCheckMessage` appends the suffix unconditionally from that field (`const stale = details.staleContinuations > 0 ? … "· measured N turn(s) ago" : ""`, goal.ts:872-873). With PI_GOAL_CHECK_EVERY > 1 an aborted due check follows one or more reuse settles (e.g. checkEvery=4: continuations 0 fresh-due, 1 and 2 reuse → age 2, 3 due → aborted), so the transcript row renders "goal check 4/10 · verify aborted — re-measuring next settle · measured 2 turn(s) ago" — a claim about a measurement the same row says did not happen.
findings.recommendation: Report `staleContinuations: 0` in the aborted details, or gate the stale suffix on `!details.aborted` in renderCheckMessage, so the aborted row states only that nothing was measured.

findings.title: A deliberate alt+x kill re-engages with `{ continue: true }` and leaves lastCheck unset, so the identical check re-runs at the next settle
findings.detail: The aborted branch now queues a notice telling the model to "end your turn, and the next settle re-measures automatically" and returns `{ continue: true }` (goal.ts:1406-1426). Because `lastCheck` stays unset and `continuations` is not incremented (the throttle computes `due = (continuations + 1) % checkEvery === 0 || !lastCheck`, goal.ts:1347), the very next settle is due again in every case where the killed check was due, so killing a check that hung (the README's "killable mid-run (alt+x)", README.md:23, and the spinner's "alt+x aborts", goal.ts:1356) costs one extra model turn and then returns the same hung verify; only `/goal pause` or `/goal stop` actually halts it. The chord therefore does not behave like the escape hatch it is advertised as for the one case it exists for — a check that wedges.
findings.recommendation: Make a deliberate kill stop the re-measure rather than immediately restoring it: e.g. park after a kill (skip the next due check, resume on the next user prompt) or require an explicit re-arm, or at minimum say in the notice/footer that the check re-runs immediately and that /goal pause|stop is the only halt.

findings.title: The new abort-notice test never asserts the message's delivery options, unlike the passing-check path
findings.detail: The kill test asserts the re-engage notice's content and details (content, aborted, ok, exitCode) but not the sendMessage options, whereas the sibling passing-check test pins them at tests/goal.test.ts:1105 (`expect(first.opts).toEqual({ deliverAs: "followUp" })`). The abort path (goal.ts:1408-1430) also returns `{ continue: true }`, so the delivery mode decides whether the notice is queued as a followUp for the continuation or delivered as a steering message; a regression to the wrong mode (or dropping the options) would still pass this test. Recommendation: assert `(sentCustom[0] as { opts: unknown }).opts` equals `{ deliverAs: "followUp" }` in the abort test.
